- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, often peaking too early and then declining too slowly — suggesting lag in recognizing price corrections.
- After sharp spikes in history (e.g., 84.90 → 87.98), model overshoots and fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is under-recognized: model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert to recent lower mean.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10–15 days of the 30d window, then gradually flatten — but true outcomes often show sharper corrections or volatility later.
- Model fails to account for sudden drops in later days (e.g., 89.30 → 77.52) — underestimates downside risk or volatility tail.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are too smooth; true outcomes show more abrupt swings, especially in last 5–10 days.
- Model tends to ignore recent low values in history when forecasting — fails to “look back” sufficiently to adjust for recent dips.
